featured_techniques.technique: Five-competency framework to drive growth in customer experience
Asset-based definition of customers and asset metric
Experience-centered leadership and outcomes in meetings
Align around onboarding, product, and purchase experiences
Build a customer listening path with multi-source feedback
Proactive reliability and innovation with a rigorous CX design methodology

concepts: cx work as reactive vs. proactive
sections.description: The speaker frames customer experience work as often reactive to survey results and announces a five-competency framework to drive growth. She introduces the idea of viewing customers as assets and creating a company-wide asset metric, then describes shifting leadership meetings to focus on outcomes and the growth implications of this reframing.
sections.title: Intro and Competency 1: Leadership language and asset-based success

sections.description: This section emphasizes aligning organizational focus around the customer experience across onboarding, product, and purchase, rather than by traditional silos (marketing, operations, sales). It highlights the shift in how a company brings a product to market and the early metrics that shape field operations.
sections.title: Competency 2: Align around experience (break silos)

sections.description: The speaker describes aggregating feedback from multiple sources (surveys, social, complaints) and mapping it to the customer journey, rather than relying solely on survey results tied to specific questions.
sections.title: Competency 3: Build a customer listening path

sections.description: This portion stresses the need for repeatable, reliable customer experiences and the ability to innovate experiences. It argues for a rigorous customer experience design approach that is as disciplined as product development to earn the customer’s story and positive social proof.
sections.title: Competency 4: Proactive experience reliability and innovation

sections.description: The final competency centers on leadership behavior: how decisions are made, how people are hired or dismissed, how unnecessary rules are removed, and whether the leadership team remains centered and committed to growth that is deliberate and aligned.
sections.title: Competency 5: Leadership decisions and deliberate growth

summary: In this short talk, Jeanne Bliss outlines a five-competency framework intended to transform customer experience work from a reactive, survey-driven activity into a growth engine for the business. She starts by reframing success around customers as assets and establishes an asset-based metric, then explains how leadership behavior and cross-functional alignment around experience (onboarding, product, and purchase) support this shift. Additional competencies cover building a comprehensive customer listening path from multiple feedback sources, instituting proactive and repeatable experience reliability with a rigorous CX design method, and ensuring leadership decisions, hiring, and policy environments align with deliberate growth. Together, these elements are presented as an organizational engine to drive sustained growth through improved customer experience.
title: Jeanne Bliss On "The Five Competencies"
